Reactome TAS ("MMAA:MUT binds AdoCbl") assigning molecular carrier activity. MMAA does not itself carry cobalamin as cargo; it is the G-protein that gates the transfer of AdoCbl (produced by MMAB) onto MMUT in a GTP-dependent manner. "Molecular carrier activity" mislabels the gating/regulatory GTPase role as direct cofactor transport.
manual_reason: MMAA is the GTPase that gates cobalamin transfer onto MMUT, not the molecular carrier of cobalamin cargo.

reactome_title: Methylation of N-acetyl-5-HT to form melatonin
reactome_display_name: Methylation of N-acetyl-5-HT to form melatonin
review_summary: TAS (Reactome) annotation to S-methyltransferase activity. This is the WRONG MOLECULAR-FUNCTION BRANCH: S-methyltransferases transfer a methyl group to a sulfur atom, whereas ASMT is definitively an O-methyltransferase (EC 2.1.1.4) that methylates the 5-hydroxyl oxygen of N-acetylserotonin. This is a Reactome-to-GO mapping artifact (the reaction consumes SAM, but the acceptor atom is oxygen, not sulfur). Not experimental. Mark as over-annotated; the correct MF is GO:0017096 / GO:0008171.
manual_reason: ASMT methylates the 5-hydroxyl oxygen of N-acetylserotonin, so the Reactome event was mapped to the sulfur-acceptor methyltransferase branch by mistake.
